apps.name: Mojave UI
apps.description: Alternative Pip-Boy interface in the style of the TV series' second season: amber New Vegas theme, faction reputation, quest log, Mojave map, Pip-OS 1.33's ID card, feeds and lists, plus FM radio presets, a media remote, notes and an inbox.

apps.name: PIP-OS X (concept)
apps.description: A futuristic take on the Pip-Boy: holographic rings and radar, S.P.E.C.I.A.L. chart, V.A.T.S. targeting, rotating wireframes, the device's own Vault Boy and map animations, Pip-OS 1.33's ID card, feeds and lists, plus FM radio presets, a media remote, notes and an inbox.

apps.name: Capital UI
apps.description: Alternative Pip-Boy interface in the style of Fallout 3: green phosphor, skills, the main quest line, the Capital Wasteland map and D.C. radio stations, Pip-OS 1.33's ID card, feeds and lists, plus FM radio presets, a media remote, notes and an inbox.

apps.name: Pip-Boy 2000
apps.description: Alternative Pip-Boy interface in the style of Fallout and Fallout 2: Vault 13, the eighteen original skills, the hunt for the water chip and a map of Southern California, plus Pip-OS 1.33's ID card, feeds and lists, FM radio presets, a media remote, notes and an inbox.

apps.name: Endurance
apps.description: A flight-deck interface based on the film Interstellar (2014): the turning ring, the crew, the robot's humor and honesty settings, the three candidate worlds, Plan A and Plan B, a time-slip calculator, a watch and the route through the wormhole, plus Pip-OS 1.33's ID card, feeds and lists, FM radio presets, a media remote, notes and an inbox. With the film's title, the black hole as it was rendered for the film, and Hamilton's Murph watch, used with permission.

apps.name: TARS
apps.description: The Pip-Boy as the robot from the film Interstellar (2014): four hinged slabs on every screen, a start-up console, humor, honesty, trust and discretion settings that decide what it says (with a cue light when it's joking), questions to ask it, a docking game and Morse code by screen flash, plus Pip-OS 1.33's ID card, feeds and lists, FM radio presets, a media remote, notes and an inbox. Its settings are shared with Endurance.

extensions.name: Media remote
extensions.description: Adds INV › REMOTE: the wheels control volume, play/pause and tracks on the computer the Pip-Boy is plugged into (USB media keys).

extensions.name: Radio presets
extensions.description: Puts your stations from the Radio presets page into the stock RADIO menu: one press tunes the Pip-Boy's FM radio.

extensions.name: Notes
extensions.description: Adds DATA › NOTES: text notes from the SD card, made on the companion's ID, lists & notes page.

extensions.name: Inbox
extensions.description: Adds STAT › INBOX to the stock interface: messages you send from the companion's Home page, kept on the SD card to read later.

holotapes.name: Terminal hacking
holotapes.description: The password puzzle from the terminals of Fallout 3, New Vegas and 4: pick the right word from eight in four attempts, with a likeness score after each guess.

holotapes.name: Lockpicking
holotapes.description: The bobby-pin lock from Fallout 3, New Vegas and 4: find the sweet spot with the wheel before your pins break. Four locks, Novice to Master.

holotapes.name: Cap Collector
holotapes.description: A small arcade game in the spirit of the holotape games: slide the crate under the falling bottle caps and keep the mini nukes out of it.

holotapes.name: FM scan
holotapes.description: Sweeps the FM band with the Pip-Boy's own radio, draws the signal strength across the dial and lists the strongest stations to tune to. Needs the stock interface.

holotapes.name: Stand clock
holotapes.description: A clock for when the Pip-Boy sits on its stand: big time, the date, and Vault-Tec, RobCo and Nuka-Cola faces. Keeps the Pip-Boy awake while USB power is connected.

holotapes.name: Level up
holotapes.description: Experience points for real tasks: every item ticked off in your lists is worth 10 XP. Earn enough and you level up, with Vault Boy and the level-up sound.
